title: Special Episode: An Interplanetary Jazz Legend, a Cosmic Vegetable and a Psychic Prodigy

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在清晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中度过的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我要测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用一个不同的起始单词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一个平底锅就能做好的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，致力于帮您理解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅即可享受特别优惠，网址是nytimes.com斜杠subscribe。

sentences.en: Hi, I am so glad you're here.
sentences.zh: 嗨，很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Severson.
sentences.zh: 我是金·塞弗森。

sentences.en: I write about food for The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》撰写美食文章。

sentences.en: I'm here to tell you about a brand new project we've been cooking up.
sentences.zh: 我来这里是想告诉你们一个我们一直在筹备的全新项目。

sentences.en: It's an audio app.
sentences.zh: 这是一个音频应用。

sentences.en: It's called NYT Audio.
sentences.zh: 它叫“纽约时报音频”。

sentences.en: And it's got all the shows you already know and love like The Daily, plus some exclusive new shows, reporters reading the articles they've written, and so much more.
sentences.zh: 这里有你已经熟知并喜爱的所有节目，比如《每日新闻》，还有一些独家的新节目、记者朗读自己撰写的文章，以及更多内容。

sentences.en: Including something I'm especially excited about, called NYT Shorts.
sentences.zh: 其中包括一个让我格外兴奋的项目，叫做“纽约时报短节目”。

sentences.en: These are little gems, nuggets of fun, delivered directly to you from our editors, reporters, and our critics.
sentences.zh: 这些都是由我们的编辑、记者和评论员直接为你送上的精美小品、趣味金句。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: I am Jay Wertham.
sentences.zh: 我是杰伊·韦瑟姆。

sentences.en: I'm Melissa Clark.
sentences.zh: 我是梅利莎·克拉克。

sentences.en: My name is Elizabeth Egan.
sentences.zh: 我叫伊丽莎白·伊根。

sentences.en: And I'm A.O.
sentences.zh: 我是A·O。

sentences.en: Scott.
sentences.zh: 斯科特。

sentences.en: My name is Yohandi Kamalafit.
sentences.zh: 我叫约罕迪·卡马拉菲特。

sentences.en: I'm Gilbert Cruz.
sentences.zh: 我是吉尔伯特·克鲁兹。

sentences.en: And I'll be here for the next few Saturdays, so you can get a taste of some of these new stories.
sentences.zh: 接下来的几个星期六我都会在这里，这样你们就能先睹为快，体验一下这些新故事。

sentences.en: Okay, here we go.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Today we have some old music for you to revisit, an ode to a very sublime vegetable, and some very cool recommendations to keep you busy this weekend.
sentences.zh: 今天我们为你准备了一些值得重温的老音乐、一首献给某种美妙蔬菜的赞歌，以及一些能让你这个周末过得充实的精彩推荐。

sentences.en: First up, my colleague Marcus Moore, who writes about music.
sentences.zh: 首先是我的同事马库斯·穆尔，他是一名音乐记者。

sentences.en: Listen, we're going to make it work.
sentences.zh: 听着，我们会搞定的。

sentences.en: It's like jazz.
sentences.zh: 这就像爵士乐。

sentences.en: It's a jazz improv, man.
sentences.zh: 老兄，这是爵士即兴演奏。

sentences.en: That's all it is.
sentences.zh: 就这么简单。

sentences.en: We're going to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 我们会想出办法的。

sentences.en: My name is Marcus J.
sentences.zh: 我叫马库斯·J。

sentences.en: Moore, and this is Five Minutes to Love Sun Ra.
sentences.zh: 穆尔，这是“给桑·拉的五分钟爱意”。

sentences.en: I always want to tell people about some good music or some good news.
sentences.zh: 我总是想跟人们分享一些好音乐或者好消息。

sentences.en: And that's why I'm here.
sentences.zh: 这就是我来到这里的原因。

sentences.en: I'm here to spread the gospel of Sun Ra.
sentences.zh: 我来这里是为了传播桑·拉的福音。

sentences.en: I'm here to talk about Space is a Place as an incredible jazz song.
sentences.zh: 我来这里是为了讨论《太空就是归宿》这首不可思议的爵士乐。

sentences.en: And hopefully these five minutes will help you fall in love with Sun Ra the way that I did.
sentences.zh: 希望这五分钟能帮你像我一样爱上桑·拉。

sentences.en: It was the year 2010.
It was the summertime.
sentences.zh: 那是夏天。

sentences.en: And somebody online was talking about Sun Ra.
sentences.zh: 网上有人在谈论桑·拉。

sentences.en: And I just wanted to see what was going on, because I thought maybe it was traditional jazz or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我只是想去看看是怎么回事，因为我觉得那可能是传统爵士乐之类的东西。

sentences.en: And the first thing that comes up is Space is the Place.
sentences.zh: 结果最先跳出来的就是《太空就是归宿》。

sentences.en: I was hooked right away, but I also was uncomfortable in a way.
sentences.zh: 我立刻就被迷住了，但同时也感到有些不自在。

sentences.en: All this atonal screeching, and you have these raucous druMs.
sentences.zh: 全都是这种无调性的刺耳声音，还有刺耳的鼓声。

sentences.en: The first thing that struck me when I heard the song was the mantra,
sentences.zh: 我听到这首歌时首先打动我的是它的咒语般的歌词，

sentences.en: Space is the Place, repeated over and over, permeating itself into your skin.
sentences.zh: “太空就是归宿”，一遍又一遍地重复着，渗透进你的皮肤里。

sentences.en: At the time, I didn't know what that meant.
sentences.zh: 当时，我并不知道这意味着什么。

sentences.en: But I like music like that that challenges me.
sentences.zh: 但我喜欢这种挑战我的音乐。

sentences.en: I like music where I may not get it on the first hit, but as long as it elicits some sort of emotion, I got to check it out.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那种可能第一遍听不懂，但只要能激起某种情绪，我就必须去探索的音乐。

sentences.en: Sun Ra was born Herman Blunt in Birmingham, Alabama.
sentences.zh: 桑·拉出生于阿拉巴马州伯明翰，原名赫曼·布朗特。

sentences.en: And he became Sun Ra following an out-of-body experience in college
sentences.zh: 他在大学期间经历了一次濒死体验后改名为桑·拉，

sentences.en: where, according to him, his body was taken over by aliens.
sentences.zh: 据他所说，当时他的身体被外星人接管了。

sentences.en: And once he had that out-of-body experience, he just sort of gradually brought in the cosmic elements to his music.
sentences.zh: 一旦有了那种濒死体验，他就开始在音乐中逐渐融入宇宙元素。

sentences.en: He believed that Black people would not find liberation on this planet and that they should seek refuge on other planets.
sentences.zh: 他坚信黑人无法在这个星球上获得解放，他们应该去其他星球寻求庇护。

sentences.en: He was operating in the 50s and 60s when he saw very clear indicators of racism,
sentences.zh: 他活跃于50和60年代，当时他看到了种族主义的非常明显的迹象，

sentences.en: Jim Crow South, you know, civil rights struggles and things of that nature.
sentences.zh: 比如吉姆·克劳南方的种族隔离，你知道的，民权斗争以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And he just, you know, instead of trying to coexist, he said, OK, let's just separate and let's just find somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他没有去尝试共存，而是说，好吧，让我们分开吧，让我们去别的地方找找。

sentences.en: You know, whereas someone like a Marcus Garvey was trying to get people to go back to West Africa, he just wanted to bypass the whole planet somehow.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像马库斯·加维那样的人试图让人们回到西非，而他只想设法绕过整个地球。

sentences.en: So that's going to come out in the music.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都会在音乐中体现出来。

sentences.en: Space is the Place is an album released by Sun Ra in 1972.
sentences.zh: 《太空就是归宿》是桑·拉于1972年发行的一张专辑。

sentences.en: And the track itself, in my estimation, is a two-part song.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这首歌本身分为两个部分。

sentences.en: In the beginning, you hear the mantra more prominent.
sentences.zh: 一开始，你会听到那个咒语更加突出。

sentences.en: You hear June Tyson singing Space is the Place over and over again as a mission statement for Sun Ra Orchestra.
sentences.zh: 你会听到琼·泰森一遍又一遍地唱着“太空就是归宿”，将其作为桑·拉管弦乐团的使命宣言。

sentences.en: But then in the second half, you have the instrumentation that takes over.
sentences.zh: 但在后半部分，器乐演奏占据了主导。

sentences.en: You hear the conga druMs.
sentences.zh: 你听到康加鼓的声音。

sentences.en: You hear the saxophones.
sentences.zh: 你听到萨克斯管的声音。

sentences.en: You hear Sun Ra playing keys.
sentences.zh: 你听到桑·拉在弹奏键盘。

sentences.en: You hear all of this stuff going on.
sentences.zh: 你听到所有这些声音交织在一起。

sentences.en: It conveys the same sense of joy and freedom that the mantra does, but it's more revivaliSt.
sentences.zh: 它传达了与那个咒语相同的喜悦和自由感，但更有一种复兴运动的感觉。

sentences.en: You know, it's based in African tradition, meaning we're just going to play.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它植根于非洲传统，意思是我们就这样演奏。

sentences.en: We're going to summon the spirits.
sentences.zh: 我们要召唤灵魂。

sentences.en: We're going to knock the dust out.
sentences.zh: 我们要抖落尘埃。

sentences.en: We're going to be free and we're going to be joyous.
sentences.zh: 我们要获得自由，我们要充满欢乐。

sentences.en: Anytime I hear that, it almost feels to me like, okay, we're taking off.
sentences.zh: 每次我听到这个，几乎都感觉像是，好吧，我们要起飞了。

sentences.en: For those of you who are looking to get into the song, I would say buckle up.
sentences.zh: 对于那些想要欣赏这首歌的人，我想说请系好安全带。

sentences.en: It's a very adventurous track, but in a good way.
sentences.zh: 这是一首非常具有冒险精神的曲子，但朝著好的方向发展。

sentences.en: Yes, it can be intimidating to hear all of this going on at the same time, but just give the music a chance.
sentences.zh: 是的，听到所有这些声音同时响起可能会让人感到畏惧，但请给这音乐一个机会。

sentences.en: Once you get into what he's talking about and once you start studying what Sun Ra was about, the rewards are astounding.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始了解他在谈论什么，一旦你开始研究桑·拉的主旨，你所获得的回报将是惊人的。

sentences.en: Sun Ra died in 1993.
sentences.zh: 桑·拉于1993年逝世。

sentences.en: He is somewhere in space, back where he belonged, among the planets, playing his organ.
sentences.zh: 他在宇宙的某个地方，回到了他属于的地方，在行星之间弹奏着他的管风琴。

sentences.en: You know, we say the phrase a lot of times, ahead of its time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们经常说“超越时代”这个词。

sentences.en: I truly think Sun Ra was ahead of his time, for sure.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为桑·拉绝对是超越了时代的。

sentences.en: And that's why he's having a revival still to this day.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么直到今天他依然引发热潮。

sentences.en: And now, from outer space, somehow that's a perfect transition to a cosmic vegetable.
sentences.zh: 现在，从外太空，这竟然完美过渡到了一种宇宙蔬菜。

sentences.en: Here's our critic at large, Tejal Rao, with a love letter.
sentences.zh: 接下来是我们的特约评论员特贾尔·拉奥带来的情书。

sentences.en: Let me tell you why I love eggplant.
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你为什么我爱茄子。

sentences.en: Grew up calling it aubergine, which is what the British call it, and the French call it.
sentences.zh: 我从小管它叫欧白茄（aubergine），英国人和法国人都是这么叫的。

sentences.en: Eggplant is a very funny, just like a funny word to me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，茄子（eggplant）是一个非常有趣、甚至搞笑的词。

sentences.en: Aubergine sort of fits it better, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得欧白茄这个词好像更贴切一点。

sentences.en: I mean, eggplant is one of the most beautiful vegetables, and the variety of eggplant is cosmic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，茄子是最美丽的蔬菜之一，而且茄子的品种简直千变万化、宇宙无垠。

sentences.en: You can get eggplant that are tiny, that are almost like beads.
sentences.zh: 你可以买到极小的茄子，长得几乎像珠子一样。

sentences.en: And then there's long, slim, bendy eggplant.
sentences.zh: 然后还有又长、又细、能弯曲的茄子。

sentences.en: There's big, you know, chubby, bulbous eggplant that look like babies.
sentences.zh: 还有那种很大、胖乎乎、圆滚滚、看起来像婴儿一样的茄子。

sentences.en: And they're in all colors.
sentences.zh: 它们有各种颜色。

sentences.en: They're soft, creamy, white.
sentences.zh: 有柔软、绵密、白色的。

sentences.en: They can be almost melon, orange.
sentences.zh: 它们甚至可以是近乎甜瓜的橙色。

sentences.en: All shades of purple, sometimes so deep that they look black.
sentences.zh: 各种深浅不一的紫色，有时深得看起来像黑色。

sentences.en: I mean, the most wonderful thing about eggplant, I think, how luxurious it can feel.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于茄子最美妙的事情，我认为是它能给人带来多么奢华的口感。

sentences.en: I didn't always like eggplant.
sentences.zh: 我以前并不总是喜欢茄子。

sentences.en: I mean, some people just don't like eggplant, so fair enough.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些人就是不喜欢茄子，这也可以理解。

sentences.en: But some people think they don't like eggplant.
sentences.zh: 但有些人以为自己不喜欢茄子。

sentences.en: But I think they've actually just experienced undercooked eggplant.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们其实只是吃过没煮熟的茄子。

sentences.en: So it still is a little bit firm and spongy, and that's so unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 所以它仍然有点硬和海绵状，那是相当令人不愉快的。

sentences.en: And generally, it just means that it hasn't been cooked long enough to get fully, thoroughly, properly tender and creamy.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这意味着它煮的时间还不够长，没能变得完全、彻底、恰到好处的软糯和绵密。

sentences.en: Here are a few really delicious different things you can make with eggplant.
sentences.zh: 这里有几种你可以用茄子做出的极其美味的不同做法。

sentences.en: So if you want ridiculously luxurious, creamy eggplant that's almost kind of starting to disappear into hot pasta and tomato sauce,
sentences.zh: 如果你想要那种荒谬般奢华、绵密的茄子，它几乎要在热腾腾的意面和番茄酱中融化消失，

sentences.en: you can make a variation of the Sicilian pasta dish, Pastela Norma.
sentences.zh: 你可以做一个西西里经典意面菜肴诺玛意面的变体。

sentences.en: Pieces of fried eggplant cooked in olive oil, so they soak up a lot of that oil.
sentences.zh: 用橄榄油炸过的茄子块，它们会吸收大量的油。

sentences.en: They get really tender.
sentences.zh: 它们变得非常软。

sentences.en: The edges get just a tiny bit crispy, mixed with tomato sauce, some cheese, fresh basil leaves, and hot pasta.
sentences.zh: 边缘变得有一点点脆，与番茄酱、一些奶酪、新鲜罗勒叶和热意面拌在一起。

sentences.en: You know, that's a really, really simple and rewarding way to cook it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是一种非常、非常简单且让人满足的烹饪方法。

sentences.en: If you want kind of a really smooth, melting texture, you should char eggplant.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要那种非常顺滑、即融的质感，你应该把茄子烤焦。

sentences.en: You know, leave it whole, just wash it, dry it, and you can either put it against a flame on your gas stove or turn it over charcoal or an electric grill
sentences.zh: 你知道的，整个烤，洗净擦干，你可以把它直接放在燃气灶的火上烤，或者在木炭或电烤架上翻转，

sentences.en: and just let the skin completely char so that it blackens and starts to flake and the eggplant gets kind of slumpy and starts to shrivel and gets very, very soft.
sentences.zh: 让表皮完全烤焦，直到变黑并开始剥落，然后茄子变得软塌塌的、开始干瘪，变得非常非常软。

sentences.en: And that smoky flavor that's on the skin kind of permeates the meat of the eggplant and it's completely perfumed and infused with it.
sentences.zh: 皮上那种烟熏味会渗透到茄子肉里，使茄子完全带有这种香味并与之融为一体。

sentences.en: That is the beginning of baba ganoush.
sentences.zh: 这就是巴巴加努什（中东烤茄泥）的开始。

sentences.en: It's really easy once the eggplant cools down a little bit to just take off that charred skin, which you don't need anymore.
sentences.zh: 茄子稍微冷却后，剥掉那些不再需要的烤焦的外皮非常简单。

sentences.en: And then you emulsify it with tahina, with sesame seed paste and olive oil, lemon, garlic.
sentences.zh: 然后你把它和芝麻酱（tahina）、芝麻酱糊、橄榄油、柠檬和大蒜一起乳化。

sentences.en: And that is sort of one of the most beautiful things you can do with eggplant.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是你对茄子能做的最美妙的事情之一。

sentences.en: It makes the most of its texture.
sentences.zh: 它最大限度地发挥了茄子的质感。

sentences.en: Finally, now that you're all nice and soothed, we have an answer to that age-old question.
sentences.zh: 最后，既然你们现在都已经放松下来了，我们有一个问题要回答这个千古难题。

sentences.en: What should I do now?
sentences.zh: 我现在该做什么？

sentences.en: NYT Shorts has a regular feature we call Staff Picks that lets you in on what our editors and reporters are spending their time on.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报短节目》有一个名为“员工精选”的常设栏目，让你了解我们的编辑和记者们都在把时间花在什么上面。

sentences.en: Here's one from a pal whose advice I always listen to.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个来自我总是听取其建议的好朋友的推荐。

sentences.en: Staff Picks.
sentences.zh: 员工精选。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Nikita Richardson, and I am a senior staff editor on the food section here at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫尼基塔·理查森，我是《纽约时报》美食版块的高级员工编辑。

sentences.en: And I also write a weekly newsletter called Where to Eat New York City about eating at restaurants and other places, carts, whatever you want to, whatever you're interested in.
sentences.zh: 我还写了一份名为《纽约市哪里吃》的每周通讯，内容关于在餐馆和其他地方、餐车吃饭，随你喜欢，只要你感兴趣的都可以。

sentences.en: Life is full of amazing things to listen to, read, watch, and I know it can be truly overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 生活充满了令人惊叹的可以听、读、看的事物，我知道这确实会让人应接不暇。

sentences.en: I'm with you on that.
sentences.zh: 这一点我深有同感。

sentences.en: So here are a few of my favorite things right now that will hopefully brighten your day.
